thread.title: Bill Gross: This is why bonds are selling off

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Bill Gross: This is why bonds are selling off

organizations.name: janus henderson global unconstrained bond fund

text:
Bonds, cheap bonds.
Investors are still grappling with some whiplash caused by a bond sell off Wednesday, which saw the biggest one-day climb in two years for the 30-year U.S. Treasury yield.
Several reasons are cited for this spike, but our call of the day comes from so-called ‘bond king’ Bill Gross, who says we should blame absent foreign buyers for driving yields higher.
See Also Political Outsiders Are Shaking Up the Midterms × “Euroland, Japanese previous buyers of 10yr Treasurys have been priced out of market due to changes in hedge costs,” the manager of the Janus Henderson Global Unconstrained Bond Fund, tweeted Wednesday.
And U.S. bonds are just not bringing it for pension funds.
“For insurance companies in Germany/Japan for instance, U.S. Treasurys yield only -. 10%/-0.1%. Lack of foreign buying at these levels likely leading to lower Treasury prices.”
Gross: (2 of 2) For Insurance companies in Germany / Japan for instance, U.S. Treasuries yield only -.10% / -.01%. Lack of foreign buying at these levels likely leading to lower Treasury prices.
— Janus Henderson U.S. (@JHIAdvisorsUS) October 3, 2018 Some may be wondering if soaring bond yields will derail the bullish run for stocks, which are jittery this morning.
Robeco fund manager Jeroen Blokland, says a gradual rise in yields, corresponding with strong U.S. data, is viewed as positive and “adds to normalization of monetary policy.
“However, the last couple of days the rise in yields has been fast and a bit unexpected. Most investors seem to be positioned for a decrease in yields. Fast rising rates brings corporate debt sustainability into play,” he said, via email.
Still, he says, investors don’t need to reach for that panic button yet. “So if rates keep rising like this I expect volatility in equity markets, but as long as they don’t ramp up to let’s say 4% or so, I think this should be seen as positive. Also the yield curve is steepening, reducing recession odds,” said Blokland.
And what’s that old saying from Berkshire Hathaway Chairman Warren Buffett? Get greedy when others get scared?
“A nice spike in U.S. yields is just what markets needed, given how quiet things had got lately. Volatility has been trending lower all year, so a little rerun of the January panic over U.S. inflation and yields would clear the deck nicely for an autumn rally in equities,” Chris Beauchamp, Chief Market Analyst at IG, tells clients in a note.
The quote Getty Images Up all night, Fed Chair Jerome Powell “Nobody wants a central banker who sleeps well. What good is that?”—That was Fed Chairman Jerome Powell during a Q&A session at an Atlantic Magazine event . He added that “everything” keeps him up at night when it comes to the economy, but also drew some attention with his comments about getting interest rates up to a “neutral” level.
